data.gender_notes: Sapphire is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word sapphirus, meaning 'blue'. In ancient Greece, sapphires were believed to symbolize wisdom, truth, and the power of the heavens. In the Bible, the term sapphire is used to describe the foundation of God's throne, symbolizing His power, wisdom, and faithfulness. The name Sapphire carries the meaning “Blue gemstone” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sapphire usually hope their child will grow to embody blue gemstone and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sapphire total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
